correctness.rationale: Reconstructed δ(x,y)=g(y)-f(x), whose image is a translate of rank-s connected subtorus W. Standard torus category yields <=s planner domains; pulling back s independent degree-one rational cohomology generators gives a nonzero cup-product, proving >=s. Every synchronized rule forces f(T^a)=g(T^b), or strict TC is infinite. When cosets agree, corestrictions are smooth surjective torus homomorphisms, hence fibrations onto common H; lift local target paths continuously, proving strict TC=s. Integer character annihilators test coset equality and Smith normal form decomposes ker(M) as T^(a+b-s) times ∏ Z/d_i. The rank-zero, zero-domain-dimension and disjoint-image cases agree. All claims follow from explicitly stated topological and lattice-algebra prerequisites; no numerical experiment is used to justify infinite dimensions.
residual_risks: Finite strict classification holds only for affine maps and exact integer matrices/torus offsets; arbitrary continuous strict TC not addressed.
Only if δ image contains zero is compatibility fibre nonempty; integer SNF must not be confused with the continuous image subgroup.

originality.rationale: FAIL on actual implication, not failed search or inaccessible literature. The relaxed part is a direct specialization of García-Calcines–Vilches Theorem8.9, TC_H(f,g)=cat(δ), using textbook rank/cohomology of torus homomorphisms; Corollary5.7 already supplies homotopy invariance. In the nonempty strict case the map factors through a common subtorus and source Proposition6.3(3) already proves strict=relaxed for its two fibrations. Unequal image cosets trivially obstruct synchronized paths by endpoints, as illustrated by the source Example6.5(1). The remainder is precisely textbook Smith-normal-form kernel decomposition and character-annihilator subgroup tests. Thus every substantive component is a routine corollary of stronger published results and standard structure theory, with no independent nonstandard lemma.
residual_risks: This is a well-organized potentially useful pedagogical arithmetic reference, but usefulness does not create a novel theorem over stronger published results.
Rejection is of the entire original as written; any genuinely new surviving theorem requires a new complete proof and scientific reassessment, not a disclaimer.
